tags: why does my dog lick their lips
script: Your dog isn't eating anything, there's no food around, and yet that tongue keeps flicking out over their lips again and again. Sometimes it really is just anticipation, a sign they smell something good nearby or expect a treat is coming. But lip licking is also one of the clearest calming signals in a dog's body language vocabulary. Dogs use small, subtle signals like this to communicate stress, uncertainty, or mild discomfort, both to other dogs and to us, often well before any more obvious sign shows up. You'll frequently see it paired with a slightly stiff body, ears pinned back, or avoiding eye contact, especially in situations like a vet visit, a loud environment, or an uncomfortable interaction with another dog or a stranger. Learning to notice it early is actually useful, it gives you a chance to remove your dog from a stressful situation before it escalates into something more obvious, like growling or trying to get away. Occasionally frequent lip licking paired with drooling or nausea points to a stomach issue worth mentioning to a vet, but in most everyday moments, it's simply your dog quietly telling you how they're feeling.
